instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each employer to file, with its updated registration statement, a statement of expenditures.
Section 101.72(B) requires updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) to be filed by the last day of January, May, and September each year, i.e., three times annually.
The statute specifies filings in January, May, and September rather than once per year, so there is no annual-only cadence.
The only periodic filing dates stated are January, May, and September, not monthly.
Quarterly filings would require four filings per year, but §101.72(B) requires only three (January, May, September).
Semiannual cadence would be two times per year, but §101.72(B) requires three filing dates (January, May, September).
The statute fixes the periodic schedule as the last day of January, May, and September, with no alternative periodic cadence described.
Section 101.73(C) requires an employer's statement to show the total amount of expenditures made by the employer during the period covered.
Expenditures include gifts and items such as food and beverages, entertainment, lodging, or transportation, and the employer must report a brief description of reportable expenditures.

When expenditures are made to or for the benefit of a particular covered official, the statement must list the official’s name, total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client—an itemized disclosure requirement.
The employer’s updated registration statement filed with the expenditure statement must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the covered period.
An employer’s updated registration statement must cover all legislative agents engaged by the employer, which necessarily identifies the engaged agents.

Section 101.72(C) states that when an employer engages more than one legislative agent, the employer files one updated registration statement containing the information required regarding all legislative agents engaged.
The initial registration statement requires the employer’s name and business address, which is principal contact information.
The initial registration statement requires the legislative agent’s name and business address, providing lobbyist contact information.
Neither the employer expenditure statement requirements nor the registration statement requirements shown mandate disclosure of the employer’s general nature of business.
Section 101.73(C) expressly excludes 'the compensation paid to legislative agents' from the definition of expenditures for employer reporting.
The updated registration statement requires listing specific bills or resolutions actively advocated, but does not require reporting the contacts made.
The initial registration statement must include a brief description of the type of legislation to which the engagement relates, which is a general-issue description.
The employer expenditure statement excludes 'expenses of maintaining office facilities,' indicating such indirect costs are not required to be reported.
The statute provisions provided require reporting expenditures and certain financial transactions but do not require disclosure of major financial contributors to the employer.
Registration statements must list agent/employer identities and legislation types/specific bills, but do not require names of bill members or sponsors.
